messages.author: 5605ce987fbf5469
messages.subject: Posterior density plots in the ra_noLA_model
parts:
Hi, thanks again for a wonderful toolbox!

I am running into a issue that I'd like to explore further and get some assistance with. I have noticed that the posterior densities from the ra_noLA model which I am using in hBayesDM toolbox have long tails, and I'm wondering if this indicates a problem with estimation in the model? For example, here is a plot of the result of running the code below with some fake data I attached that has a random uniform distribution of accepting and not accepting each gamble, 4 different amounts from 10-40, and 5 probabilities, just to test out how well it can estimate the parameters. I am wondering if the bump at the end of this plot of the posterior estimates indicates problems with convergence for the model? Similarly, I've attached the histogram for the model (from stan_hist) which seems to have a peak of values around 2.0, and the trace plots for the rho parameter (from stan_trace) also look unusual. 

This is the code I used to estimate the model:
library(hBayesDM)
output <- ra_noLA(data = '5subj_fake_data_4vals_5probs.txt', niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 3, ncore = 3,max_treedepth=20)
plotInd(output, "rho") 
























The same model with double the amount of simulated data:
























I'm wondering a few things: how problematic is the wide estimate for posterior densities for estimating the rho parameter with the hBayesDM toolbox? If it is problematic, is there a way I can improve the model's ability to estimate the parameter? I'm doing this simulation as a check to make sure that I am including enough gambling trials in an experiment to get a good rho estimate. I'm also interested in doing tests to see if the rho estimates in different conditions are significantly different from each other, and these wide estimates for the posterior are concerning. Further, I tried this out with more simulated data, expecting that more trials would improve the fit, and when I use 2 times the amount of trials or 4 times the amount of trials compared to the first plot I still see similar issues in the plots (see the attached figure using the same model with 2 times the amount of data). I also tried a greater range of values (6 values) and have noticed similar looking posterior densities. Any suggestions you have on improving the ability of the model to estimate the rho parameter would be much appreciated!

Thanks again,
Jessica

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Posterior density plots in the ra_noLA_model
parts:
Hi Jessica,


This is likely because rho in the model you are using is bounded between 0 and 2. Since your simulated data are random, I assume that MCMC is just exploring the entire range of rho, and subsequently getting caught at either end of the parameter space when the likelihood in between is so low (as it should be with random data). 


If you try simulating data from the data generating model with rho in [0, 2], the model should be able to estimate true rho just fine. Alternatively, you could modify the stan code to allow rho to vary in [0, Inf] (e.g., through an exponential transform as opposed to the rescaled probit transform). That said, with random data the estimates for that model would likely still lead to large variation in estimates for rho. 


Let me know if this is all clear! 


Best,

Nate
